**Answer: 7**

**Setting up the lattice count.** Let $m = ap+3b$ and $n = 2a+qb$, with $m,n$ positive integers. The map $(a,b)\mapsto(m,n)$ is linear with matrix $\begin{pmatrix}p&3\\2&q\end{pmatrix}$ and determinant $D=pq-6$.

If $D\neq 0$, the open square $(0,1)^2$ maps bijectively onto the open parallelogram with vertices $(0,0)$, $(p,2)$, $(3,q)$, $(p+3,q+2)$. Each lattice point $(m,n)$ inside this parallelogram gives exactly one valid $(a,b)$. Since $p,q\ge 1$, the parallelogram lies in the open positive quadrant, so the positivity of $m$ and $n$ is automatic.

**Degenerate case.** If $pq=6$, the image is a line segment and the solution set is infinite (for example, $(p,q)=(3,2)$ gives the whole segment $a+b=1$). So these pairs do not give exactly 14 solutions, and $D\neq 0$.

**Pick's theorem.** The parallelogram has area $A=|pq-6|$. Its boundary lattice points number $B = 2\gcd(p,2)+2\gcd(3,q)$. Pick's theorem $A = I + \tfrac{B}{2} - 1$ gives

$$I = |pq-6| - \gcd(p,2) - \gcd(3,q) + 1.$$

Setting $I=14$ gives $|pq-6| = 13+\gcd(p,2)+\gcd(3,q)$. Since $\gcd(p,2)\in\{1,2\}$ and $\gcd(3,q)\in\{1,3\}$, there are four cases. Because $pq>0$, the only option is $pq-6 = +(\text{that value})$.

| $\gcd(p,2)$ | $\gcd(3,q)$ | Required $pq$ | Valid $(p,q)$ | Count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (p odd) | 1 (3∤q) | 21 | $(3,7)$, $(21,1)$ | 2 |
| 1 (p odd) | 3 (3∣q) | 23 | none (neither 1 nor 23 is divisible by 3) | 0 |
| 2 (p even) | 1 (3∤q) | 22 | $(2,11)$, $(22,1)$ | 2 |
| 2 (p even) | 3 (3∣q) | 24 | $(2,12)$, $(4,6)$, $(8,3)$ | 3 |

Spot checks: for $(3,7)$, $|D|=15$ and $I=15-1-1+1=14$. For $(2,12)$, $|D|=18$ and $I=18-2-3+1=14$.

Total: $2+0+2+3 = 7$.

ANSWER: 7
